· 14th January 1996 means 1995 years and days from January 1, 1996 to January 14th, 1996.

· Odd no. of days in first 1600 years is 0.

· Odd number of days in 300 years is 1.

· From 1901 to 1995 there are twenty-three leap years and Seventy-two ordinary years.

· Hence, Odd no. of Days = 72 + (23 X 2) = 72 + 46 = 118 (16 weeks 6 days) = 6 odd days.

· No. of days from January 1, 1990 to January 14th, 1990, = 14 days = 0 odd days (14/7 and remainder is the odd days).

· Total odd days = 0+1+6+0 = 7 (which 7 odd days)

· 7 odd days means Sunday.

So, it will be Sunday 14th January 1996.

questions.q_en:
Read the following questions and decide which of the given statements is/are sufficient.

Question:

H, K, M, Q, U and Z are sitting around the corners of a hexagonal table. All are facing towards the centre of a table. Who is sitting fourth to the left of H?

Statements:

I. M is sitting immediately between U and Z.

II. K is sitting immediately between H and Q, who is to the immediate right of Z.
options_en: I alone is sufficient while II alone is not sufficient to answer the question.
Both I and II are together sufficient to answer the question.
II alone is sufficient while I alone is not sufficient to answer the question.
Both I and II are together are not sufficient to answer the question.
questions.solution_en:
H, K, M, Q, U and Z are sitting around the corners of a hexagonal table. All are facing towards the centre of a table.

From I alone:

M is sitting immediately between U and Z

So, no definite answer can be concluded.

Thus, I alone is not sufficient.

From II alone:

K is sitting immediately between H and Q, who is to the immediate right of Z.

So, no definite answer can be concluded.

Thus, II alone is not sufficient.

From both I and II together:

M is sitting immediately between U and Z.

So, M is sitting fourth to the left of H.

So, both I and II together is sufficient to answer the question.
questions.solution_hi:
H, K, M, Q, U and Z are sitting around the corners of a hexagonal table. All are facing towards the centre of a table.

From I alone:

M is sitting immediately between U and Z

So, no definite answer can be concluded.

Thus, I alone is not sufficient.

From II alone:

K is sitting immediately between H and Q, who is to the immediate right of Z.

So, no definite answer can be concluded.

Thus, II alone is not sufficient.

From both I and II together:

M is sitting immediately between U and Z.

So, M is sitting fourth to the left of H.

So, both I and II together is sufficient to answer the question.

questions.q_en:
In this question, there are two statements showing the relation, followed by three conclusions i, ii and iii. Assuming that the given story is true, find out which conclusion is definitely true.

Statement:

E > K = S; J < D = S ; J > G ≥ V

Conclusion:

i) V < E

ii) D = K

iii) G ≤ S
questions.solution_en:
E > K = S; J < D = S ; J > G ≥ V which is E > K = S = D > J > G ≥ V

i) V < E ; E > K = S = D > J > G ≥ V ----- Follow

ii) D = K; K = S = D --- Follow

iii) G ≤ S; S = D > J > G --- does not follow

So, Only i and ii follow
questions.solution_hi:
E > K = S; J < D = S ; J > G ≥ V which is E > K = S = D > J > G ≥ V

i) V < E ; E > K = S = D > J > G ≥ V ----- Follow

ii) D = K; K = S = D --- Follow

iii) G ≤ S; S = D > J > G --- does not follow

So, Only i and ii follow

questions.q_en: In a row of few students P was standing 17th from the left end and 23rd from the right end. If Q was standing exactly in the middle of the row, what was his rank from the left end. Assume people were facing the north.
questions.solution_en:
Total number of persons in a row= position from left + position from the right-1= 17+23-1 = 39

Hence there were 39 students in the row

Q was exactly in the middle of the row

Q's rank= (39+1)/2 =20th
